title: Microsoft Purview: lifecycle status controls for adaptive scope recipients and site owners
summary: Hold: the briefing still treats the supported relative-date attributes as an open question, but Microsoft Learn now publishes them. The lifecycle-control documentation gap remains genuine, and both cited PowerShell references opened successfully; the licensing model and membership-review path also need minor corrections.

claims.claim: The notice says the advanced query builder will support ISO 8601 durations for selected date attributes.

claims.fix: Keep the notice attribution, but add: 'Microsoft Learn now documents relative date filters in the advanced query builder; the roadmap and MC1450128 still give the rollout targets above.' The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes now has a Use relative date filters section, so the briefing should report both sources rather than present that behaviour solely as a future notice description.

claims.where: controls[0]; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No lifecycle-status setting or its UI path or automation is documented in the checked adaptive-scope guidance and references.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status recipients site owners include inactive soft deleted portal PowerShell; opened Adaptive scopes, relative-date filters, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope. None documents the lifecycle selector or a lifecycle parameter.

claims.claim: The existing query UI is Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... select + Create scope. ... assign an administrative unit. ... Select the type of scope ... Alternatively, you can select Advanced query builder

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <name> -LocationType User -RawQuery <OPATH query> creates an existing user adaptive scope in advanced query mode.
claims.quote:
New-AdaptiveScope
    -Name <String>
    -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType>
    -RawQuery <String>
The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode. You use OPATH filter syntax for advanced query mode.

claims.claim: Scope membership review is reached at Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Scope details in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... Select an existing adaptive scope from the list. ... From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].ui.path and the corresponding rendered path to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Details > Scope details'. Details is a flyout heading, not an additional selection.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <scope name> -State Added retrieves current scope members, and State can also select removed members.
claims.quote:
Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Added
This example retrieves the current members of the adaptive scope US Finance Users.
Added: Current members of the adaptive scope.
Removed: Former members of the adaptive scope.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: IsInactiveMailbox in the advanced query builder is a documented way to exclude or target inactive mailboxes.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes. For this configuration, use the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox

claims.claim: The creation wizard offers Full directory when not restricting the adaptive scope by administrative unit, and Users is the user scope choice.
claims.quote: If you don't want to restrict the adaptive scope by using administrative units, or your organization hasn't configured administrative units, keep the default of Full directory. ... first select Users as the scope type.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A role group containing Scope Manager can create an adaptive scope.
claims.quote: Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Learn lists Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Organization Management, Records Management, Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins as built-in groups containing Scope Manager.
claims.quote:
The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups:
- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Organization Management
- Records Management
- Communication Compliance
- Communication Compliance Admins

claims.claim: The New-AdaptiveScope reference requires assigned Security & Compliance PowerShell permissions and points to Purview compliance portal permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions. For more information, see Permissions in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: The scope membership UI shows Added for members currently in scope.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope

claims.claim: The membership UI shows Removed for previous members that no longer match the query.
claims.quote: Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.claim: Adaptive scope queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Queries can take up to five days to fully populate, so Learn advises waiting before attaching a new scope to a policy.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.claim: The member details list can take up to five days to show added or removed members.
claims.quote: It might take up to five days for the member details list to update added or removed members.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated lifecycle-selector-specific evaluation timing.
claims.quote: Searched: "adaptive scopes" "lifecycle" "five days"; read Adaptive scopes, relative-date filters and MC1450128. The pages state general query/member-list delays but do not describe evaluation timing for the planned lifecycle selector.

claims.claim: A role specifically authorised to change the new lifecycle selector has not been stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "adaptive scopes" "lifecycle" "role" "default"; read Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope, Set-AdaptiveScope and MC1450128. Scope creation permissions are documented, but no lifecycle-selector-specific permission is described.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the supplied notice describes a new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

claims.claim: The supplied feature descriptions do not describe an agent or autonomous action mechanism.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners, helping ensure policy targeting and scope membership remain aligned with organizational requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice does not separately describe scripted scope creation or distinguish PowerShell defaults from portal defaults.
claims.quote:
For newly created adaptive scopes:
- Active recipients and site owners will be evaluated by default.
- Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

claims.claim: The notice does not map its recipient and site-owner lifecycle controls individually to the three adaptive scope types.
claims.quote: This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

claims.claim: Learn does not document an IsInactiveMailbox-equivalent selector that includes soft-deleted recipients or evaluates site-owner lifecycle status.
claims.quote: Searched: "adaptive scopes" "soft-deleted" "site owners" "filter" and "PowerShell"; read Adaptive scopes, relative-date filters, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope. WhenSoftDeleted is a date filter, not an eligibility or site-owner lifecycle selector.
